2	name: xray-selection-low-ipm-exclusion
3	description: Low-flux (small ipm2) shot exclusion — an AGENT-DECIDED step. The agent examines the ipm2 distribution and downstream plan, then decides whether to exclude near-zero-flux shots and where to place the threshold. Mandatory before any per-shot flux normalization (division by a near-zero, noise-dominated monitor value explodes); optional but recommended for plain sums (pure SNR gain). Grounded in Run0475 evidence.
4	---
5	
6	# Selection · Method 1a — Low-ipm2 exclusion (agent decides)
7	
8	**Level:** whole shots. **Part of:** [selection](README.md).
9	**Split from** the old `01_shot_flux_quality.md`: low-side and high-side cuts are separate
10	decisions with different physics — do not couple them.
11	
12	## The decision the agent owns
13	
14	> **Run this exclusion or not? And if yes, where does the threshold go?**
15	>
16	> This is not a fixed pipeline stage. The agent gathers the evidence below, decides, and
17	> records the decision with its rationale. Skipping is a valid outcome — but must be an
18	> *explicit, recorded* choice, never a default.
19	
20	## Principle
21	
22	Shots with near-zero incident flux carry detector readout noise but almost no photons.
23	Adding them to a sum adds variance without signal; dividing by their monitor value
24	(normalization) amplifies noise unboundedly, because at zero beam the monitor reading is
25	its own electronic noise — small, often **negative**.
26	
27	## Evidence to gather before deciding (all cheap, smalldata-only)
28	
29	1. **ipm2 histogram** — look for a near-zero pile separated by a gap from the main body.
30	2. **`lightStatus/xray`** — dropped (x-ray off) shots always go; the question is the
31	   remaining "nominally on but near-zero" shots.
32	3. **Monitor zero offset** — median ipm2 over x-ray-off shots (Run0475: +4.5, i.e. 0.12 %
33	   of the median; subtract before any thresholding or ratio).
34	4. **Photon-yield spot check** — photon pixels (7–12 keV) per shot for a few low vs
35	   normal shots.
36	5. **Downstream plan** — will any step divide by a per-shot monitor (normalization,
37	   weighting)? If yes, this exclusion stops being optional.
38	
39	## Evidence from Run0475 (why the default is RUN)
40	
41	394 shots (12.3 % of the run) had xray on but ipm2 < 200:
42	
43	| Metric | low group (394) | normal group (394 sampled) |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| photon pixels / shot (median) | **41** (mostly fake — fixed hot-ish pixels) | **6448** |
46	| total photon yield | 0.73 % of the normal group | — |
47	| sample_diode | median **−0.0002**; ≤ 0 in **321/394** | +0.0019 |
48	| group mean I(q) | no rings; systematic negative high-q tail (pedestal drift) | LaB6 rings |
49	
50	Removing them: signal −0.3 %, noise variance −12.3 % → **~6 % SNR gain for free**, and it
51	removes a *systematic* (q-dependent) contamination, not just white noise.
52	
53	## Decision rules
54	
55	**Decide RUN when any of these hold**
56	- The histogram shows a near-zero pile (it does on Run0475);
57	- any downstream step divides by ipm2 or sample_diode → **mandatory** (321/394 low shots
58	  have diode ≤ 0; one such shot can destroy a whole bin);
59	- per-shot ratios/weights will be formed → threshold should move up to the start of the
60	  monitor's **linear plateau** (Run0475: det/ipm2 ratio is flat only above ipm2 ≈ 3000;
61	  below, the ratio is biased +50 %).
62	
63	**Decide SKIP when all of these hold**
64	- Distribution is unimodal with no near-zero pile, AND
65	- the only product is an unweighted diagnostic sum (shape barely affected), AND
66	- statistics are so scarce that a 12 % frame loss matters more than a 6 % SNR gain.
67	
68	**Threshold placement (if RUN)**
69	- Plain sums: anywhere in the gap between pile and body (Run0475: 200 — insensitive).
70	- Before per-shot division: start of the linear plateau (Run0475: ≈ 3000 ≈ 0.8×median).
71	- Always threshold on offset-corrected ipm2.
72	
73	## Record the decision
74	
75	Log: run/skip, threshold, shots kept/rejected (counts and %), and the one-line rationale
76	(e.g. "near-zero pile of 418 shots at <200; normalization planned → excluded"). Silent
77	truncation is the enemy of reproducibility.
78	
79	## Feeds
80	
81	[normalization § per-shot-flux](../normalization/01_per_shot_flux_ipm2.md) (which must not
82	see excluded shots) · [selection § correlation gate](05_correlation_gate.md).
83	
84	## Companion
85	
86	High-side cut is a separate decision: [01b_high_ipm_exclusion.md](01b_high_ipm_exclusion.md).
87

2	name: xray-selection-high-ipm-exclusion
3	description: High-flux (large ipm2) shot exclusion — an AGENT-DECIDED step. The agent checks for detector/monitor nonlinearity at the bright end (ratio droop, gain-mode switching, saturation) and decides whether to cut the bright tail and at what percentile. On Run0475 the evidence for harm is weak (linear to p99, no signal-driven gain switching), so this cut is protective / baseline-compatibility rather than evidence-driven — skipping is a legitimate outcome.
4	---
5	
6	# Selection · Method 1b — High-ipm2 exclusion (agent decides)
7	
8	**Level:** whole shots. **Part of:** [selection](README.md).
9	**Split from** the old `01_shot_flux_quality.md`: the bright-side cut has *different physics*
10	(saturation/nonlinearity) than the low-side cut (noise amplification) and deserves its own
11	decision.
12	
13	## The decision the agent owns
14	
15	> **Cut the bright tail or not? And if yes, at which percentile / absolute level?**
16	>
17	> Unlike the low cut, the case for this one is *conditional*: it protects against
18	> nonlinearity that may or may not be present. The agent must look for actual evidence of
19	> harm before spending statistics — the brightest shots carry the most photons.
20	
21	## Principle
22	
23	Very bright shots can exceed the linear range of (a) the detector front-end — pixels start
24	switching gain mode (G0→G1) mid-signal, (b) the intensity monitor itself, or (c) downstream
25	assumptions (e.g. one-photon counting). If any of that happens, the brightest shots distort
26	the flux-referenced result and should be dropped (or handled specially). If none of it
27	happens, cutting them only throws away the highest-SNR frames.
28	
29	## Evidence to gather before deciding
30	
31	1. **Ratio flatness at the top**: bin `det_total / ipm2` by ipm2; a droop in the top bins
32	   = detector or monitor rolling over. (Run0475: flat at ~22×10⁻⁶ from ipm2 ≈ 3700 all the
33	   way to the p99 cut — **no droop**.)
34	2. **Gain-mode switching on bright shots**: fraction of pixels with gain bits ≠ G0 among
35	   the brightest shots. (Run0475: switching pixels are a fixed set of 566 stuck/bad pixels;
36	   even 12 597-photon shots stay in G0 — LaB6 signal is ~10⁻² photons/pixel, orders below
37	   the ~34-photon G0 headroom.)
38	3. **Monitor spec/saturation**: does ipm2 clip or curve at the observed maxima?
39	4. **Baseline compatibility**: the human baseline (Taekeun) rejected the top 1 % (`p99`)
40	   before its 100-shot calibration sum. Reproducing that baseline requires the same cut.
41	
42	## Decision rules
43	
44	**Decide RUN when any of these hold**
45	- The det/ipm2 ratio droops in the top percentiles (nonlinearity observed);
46	- signal-driven gain switching appears on bright shots (not just stuck pixels);
47	- the monitor saturates below the brightest observed values;
48	- the task is to **reproduce the human baseline** → use its exact convention (p99).
49	
50	**Decide SKIP when all of these hold**
51	- Linearity holds to the top (Run0475: it does);
52	- no signal-driven gain switching (Run0475: none);
53	- statistics are precious and the product benefits from the brightest frames.
54	
55	**Cut placement (if RUN)**
56	- Percentile form (`p99`, `p99.5`) adapts to run brightness; absolute form is better when
57	  the physical saturation level is known. Record which convention and why.
58	
59	## Run0475 verdict (worked example)
60	
61	Evidence-driven answer: **SKIP is defensible** (32 shots above p99 are linear and clean);
62	baseline-compatibility answer: **RUN at p99** to match Taekeun's sum. The agent must pick
63	based on the goal of the current task and *say so* in the decision log — this is exactly the
64	kind of judgment this skill set exists to make explicit.
65	
66	## Record the decision
67	
68	Log: run/skip, convention (percentile/absolute), shots rejected, and rationale, e.g.
69	"reproducing baseline → p99 (32 shots dropped)" or "linearity verified to max → no cut".
70	
71	## Companion
72	
73	Low-side cut is a separate decision: [01a_low_ipm_exclusion.md](01a_low_ipm_exclusion.md).

2	name: xray-normalization-per-shot-flux
3	description: Per-shot incident-flux (ipm2) normalization — an AGENT-DECIDED step. The agent runs a cheap bin-consistency test (chronological bins, CV with vs without normalization) and decides whether to normalize, with which monitor, and in which form (per-shot division vs ratio-of-sums). Evidence on Run0475 - bin-to-bin CV 6.03%→3.55%; decision was NORMALIZE. Mandatory prerequisite - low-ipm exclusion. Includes the harmonic-vs-arithmetic-mean reference subtlety.
4	---
5	
6	# Normalization · Method 1 — Per-shot incident-flux (ipm2) normalization (agent decides)
7	
8	**Acts on:** shot ↔ shot. **Part of:** [normalization](README.md). **The load-bearing one.**
9	
10	## The decision the agent owns
11	
12	> **Normalize or not? With which monitor? In which form?**
13	>
14	> Do not apply this step by reflex, and do not skip it by reflex. The agent runs the
15	> evidence test below (seconds, smalldata-only), decides, and records the decision.
16	> On Run0475 the evidence said **normalize** — but the point of this file is the test,
17	> not the answer.
18	
19	## Principle
20	
21	The FEL's per-shot incident flux `I0` fluctuates ~100 % shot-to-shot and drifts over
22	minutes. The physical observable is scattering *per incident photon*, so each shot is
23	divided by its own flux before combining:
24	
25	```
26	n_i  = ipm2c_i / ⟨ipm2c⟩_kept        # offset-corrected, dimensionless, mean 1
27	S(q) = Σ_i f_i(q) / n_i              # per-shot division   (needs linear-plateau shots only)
28	S(q) = Σ_i f_i(q) / Σ_i n_i          # ratio-of-sums form  (robust to monitor noise)
29	```
30	
31	`ipm2c = ipm2 − offset`, offset = median ipm2 over x-ray-off shots (Run0475: +4.5).
32	
33	## The evidence test (run this before deciding)
34	
35	1. Keep only shots passing [01a low-ipm exclusion](../selection/01a_low_ipm_exclusion.md)
36	   at the linear-plateau threshold.
37	2. Split kept shots into ~8 **chronological** bins (mimics how delay scans sample time).
38	3. Compute each bin's mean I(q); compare bin-to-bin CV of total intensity, with vs
39	   without dividing each shot by `n_i`.
40	4. Sanity anchors: correlation of per-shot detector total with the monitor; ratio
41	   flatness across the intensity range.
42	
43	### Run0475 results (worked example)
44	
45	| Test | unnormalized | normalized by ipm2 |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| chronological bins (the realistic case) | CV 6.03 % | **3.55 %** |
48	| intensity-sorted bins (pure-flux control) | 61.5 % | 2.15 % |
49	| random bins (drift hidden — underestimates value) | 2.99 % | 2.42 % |
50	| per-shot CV, brighter half | 63 % | 45 % (identical to sample_diode's 45 %) |
51	
52	det~ipm2 r = 0.841 ≈ det~sample_diode r = 0.840; Poisson floor for these bins ≈ 0.09 %,
53	so the removed spread was systematic drift, not counting noise.
54	**Decision on Run0475: NORMALIZE** (flux-driven half of the drift removed; residual
55	~3.5 % is pointing/spectral drift that no monitor division can remove — that residual is
56	what pump-on/off referencing is for).
57	
58	## Decision rules
59	
60	**Decide NORMALIZE when any of these hold**
61	- The bin test shows a material CV drop (it did: 6.0 → 3.5 %);
62	- subsets of shots will be compared (delay bins, on/off groups, run-to-run) —
63	  for pump–probe this is **mandatory**, difference signals are ≪ the 6 % drift;
64	- monitor correlates with the detector total (r ≳ 0.8) over the kept shots.
65	
66	**Decide SKIP when all of these hold**
67	- The only product is a single static sum used for geometry/masking (normalization
68	  leaves the shape unchanged — per-pixel corr 0.985 on Run0475);
69	- or the monitor is broken/uncorrelated on this run (dividing by a bad monitor *injects*
70	  noise — this is why the test comes first, and why skipping must be possible).
71	
72	**Form and monitor choice (if normalizing)**
73	- Shots restricted to the monitor's linear plateau → per-shot division is safe;
74	  otherwise prefer ratio-of-sums.
75	- ipm2 (upstream) vs sample_diode: statistically equivalent here (45 % vs 45 %), but
76	  ipm2 is upstream of the sample — safe for pump–probe, whereas a post-sample diode can
77	  divide out the pump-induced signal itself. Default: ipm2.
78	
79	## Hard prerequisite
80	
81	[Low-ipm exclusion](../selection/01a_low_ipm_exclusion.md) **must run first**: near-zero
82	shots have monitor readings that are pure noise (often negative — 321/394 low shots on
83	Run0475 had sample_diode ≤ 0); dividing by them destroys bins. A guard against NaN/0 is
84	not sufficient — it does not catch −0.0002.
85	
86	## Reference-convention subtlety (important)
87	
88	`Σwf/Σw` with `w = ⟨ipm2⟩/ipm2` is algebraically referenced to the **harmonic-mean** flux;
89	a plain mean references the **arithmetic mean**. On Run0475 this is a constant ×0.63
90	rescale (HM/AM = 5213/8264), *not* a physical difference — multiply by AM/HM to compare.
91	
92	## Record the decision
93	
94	Log: normalize yes/no, monitor, form, offset used, kept-shot definition, the bin-test
95	numbers that justified it, and the residual CV (hand it to the QA/differencing stage).
96	
97	## Repo
98	
99	`weighted_sum_v2.py`, `Normalization_method.md`, `Normalization_方法与对比.md`,
100	`run475_weighted_sum.npy`, `run475_pershot_weights.npy`.

4	- `shot_table.npz` — per-shot columns, global time order (same order as frames):

6	  xray (1 = beam, from EVR code 137/162), laser (1 = on, code 90/91),
7	  det_total (summed calibrated keV over good pixels),

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Step 2 (deterministic executor): apply the agent's decisions.json, then accumulate.
3	
4	Reads outputs/<run>/decisions.json (written by the reduction agent), builds the
5	keep-mask and per-shot weights from npy/shot_table.npz, streams frames from the
6	npy/frames_raw.npy memmap, calibrates each kept frame, and writes:
7	
8	  outputs/<run>/sum_calib.npy      (2, 512, 1024) float64 — (weighted) calib sum
9	  outputs/<run>/sum_assembled.npy  (1064, 1030)  float64 — psana geometry via calib/ix,iy
10	  outputs/<run>/sum.png            robust-scaled preview for the mask agent
11	  outputs/<run>/accumulate_log.json  counts + settings, the provenance record
12	
13	decisions.json schema (all fields required; "rationale" free text):
14	{
15	  "selection": {
16	    "require_xray_on": true,
17	    "low_ipm_exclusion":  {"run": true,  "threshold": 3000.0, "rationale": "..."},
18	    "high_ipm_exclusion": {"run": false, "percentile": 99.0,  "rationale": "..."}
19	  },
20	  "normalization": {
21	    "run": true, "monitor": "ipm2", "form": "per_shot",   # or "ratio_of_sums" / no-op
22	    "offset": "auto",                                      # or a number
23	    "rationale": "..."
24	  }
25	}
26	"""
27	
28	from __future__ import annotations
29	
30	import argparse
31	import json
32	import sys
33	import time
34	from pathlib import Path
35	
36	import numpy as np
37	
38	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
39	from xtclib import calibrate
40	
41	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
42	
43	
44	def main() -> int:
45	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
46	    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", required=True, help="outputs/<run> dir holding decisions.json")
47	    args = ap.parse_args()
48	    out = Path(args.out_dir)
49	    dec = json.loads((out / "decisions.json").read_text())
50	
51	    t = np.load(ROOT / "npy/shot_table.npz")
52	    ipm2, xray = t["ipm2"], t["xray"]
53	    N = len(ipm2)
54	
55	    sel = dec["selection"]
56	    keep = np.ones(N, bool)
57	    if sel.get("require_xray_on", True):
58	        keep &= xray == 1
59	
60	    off_cfg = dec["normalization"].get("offset", "auto")
61	    offset = float(np.median(ipm2[xray == 0])) if off_cfg == "auto" else float(off_cfg)
62	    ipm2c = ipm2 - offset
63	
64	    low = sel["low_ipm_exclusion"]
65	    if low["run"]:
66	        keep &= ipm2c > float(low["threshold"])
67	    high = sel["high_ipm_exclusion"]
68	    if high["run"]:
69	        keep &= ipm2 < np.percentile(ipm2[xray == 1], float(high["percentile"]))
70	
71	    norm = dec["normalization"]
72	    weights = np.ones(N)
73	    if norm["run"]:
74	        if norm.get("monitor", "ipm2") != "ipm2":
75	            print(f"[warn] monitor {norm['monitor']} not in shot_table; falling back to ipm2",
76	                  file=sys.stderr)
77	        mono = ipm2c.copy()
78	        bad = keep & ~(mono > 0)
79	        if bad.any():                       # normalization must never divide by <=0
80	            keep &= mono > 0
81	            print(f"[guard] dropped {int(bad.sum())} kept shots with monitor <= 0", file=sys.stderr)
82	        if norm.get("form", "per_shot") == "per_shot":
83	            weights[keep] = mono[keep].mean() / mono[keep]
84	        # ratio_of_sums: accumulate plain, record divisor in the log instead
85	
86	    ped = np.load(ROOT / "calib/ped.npy")
87	    gain = np.load(ROOT / "calib/gain.npy")
88	    frames = np.load(ROOT / "npy/frames_raw.npy", mmap_mode="r")
89	
90	    t0 = time.time()
91	    s = np.zeros((2, 512, 1024))
92	    kept_idx = np.where(keep)[0]
93	    for k, i in enumerate(kept_idx):
94	        s += weights[i] * calibrate(np.asarray(frames[i]), ped, gain)
95	        if (k + 1) % 500 == 0:
96	            print(f"[accumulate] {k+1}/{len(kept_idx)} ({time.time()-t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
97	
98	    np.save(out / "sum_calib.npy", s)
99	    ix = np.load(ROOT / "calib/ix.npy").astype(np.intp)
100	    iy = np.load(ROOT / "calib/iy.npy").astype(np.intp)
101	    img = np.zeros((1064, 1030))
102	    img[ix, iy] = s
103	    np.save(out / "sum_assembled.npy", img)
104	
105	    import matplotlib
106	    matplotlib.use("Agg")
107	    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
108	    nz = img[img != 0]
109	    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 9.5))
110	    im = ax.imshow(img, cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=np.percentile(nz, 99.5),
111	                   interpolation="nearest")
112	    ax.set_title(f"{out.name}: sum of {len(kept_idx)} kept shots"
113	                 f" ({'normalized' if norm['run'] else 'plain'})")
114	    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.85, label="summed keV")
115	    fig.savefig(out / "sum.png", dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
116	
117	    log = {
118	        "n_events": int(N),
119	        "kept": int(keep.sum()),
120	        "rejected": int(N - keep.sum()),
121	        "ipm2_offset": offset,
122	        "weights_range": [float(weights[keep].min()), float(weights[keep].max())]
123	        if keep.any() else None,
124	        "ratio_of_sums_divisor": float(ipm2c[keep].sum())
125	        if norm["run"] and norm.get("form") == "ratio_of_sums" else None,
126	        "sum_total_keV": float(s.sum()),
127	        "elapsed_s": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
128	        "decisions_echo": dec,
129	    }
130	    (out / "accumulate_log.json").write_text(json.dumps(log, indent=2))
131	    print(f"[done] kept {log['kept']}/{N}, sum written to {out}", flush=True)
132	    return 0
133	
134	
135	if __name__ == "__main__":
136	    raise SystemExit(main())

Use to clean an isotropic/amorphous/powder background where azimuthal symmetry holds. Warning — it removes real anisotropic (single-crystal/texture) signal.
4	---
5	
6	# Masking · Method 2 — pyFAI azimuthal sigma-clipping (signal-based)
7	
8	**Family:** signal-dependent. **Part of:** [masking](README.md).
9	
10	## Principle
11	
12	Diffraction has azimuthal (χ) symmetry: pixels on the same `q` ring should read similar
13	intensity. Iterate per ring — compute robust mean μ_q and std σ_q, clip pixels with
14	`|I − μ_q| > thres·σ_q`, recompute, repeat. Then back-project the 1D clean model to 2D via
15	`calcfrom1d` and flag any pixel with `dev = |I − mean_2D| / std_2D > thres`.
16	
17	```
18	for each q-ring:  μ_q, σ_q = robust mean/std;  drop |I-μ_q| > thres·σ_q;  iterate ≤ max_iter
19	mask = ( |I_pixel - mean_2D(q)| / std_2D(q) ) > thres
20	```
21	
22	## Parameters (tested values, and why)
23	
24	| Param | Value | Why |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| `thres` | 3.0 | Standard 3σ clip — balance removing outliers vs keeping signal. Smaller ⇒ more aggressive. |
27	| `max_iter` | 5 | Usually converged by 5; more over-clips real peaks. |
28	| `error_model` | `azimuthal` | Use in-ring variance, **not** Poisson — data are averaged ADU, not photon counts. |
29	| `npt_radial` | 122 | Matches the file's native azav q-grid (Δq ≈ 0.02 Å⁻¹) for direct comparison. |
30	| `radial_range` | [0.0, 2.44] Å⁻¹ | Covers the detector's full valid q. |
31	| `method` | `("no","csr","cython")` | `no` pixel-splitting is **required** — splitting puts one pixel in several rings and breaks the clip logic. |
32	| `correctSolidAngle` | True | Standard flat-detector correction (see [normalization](../normalization/03_solid_angle_correction.md)). |
33	| `polarization_factor` | None | Off in this demo to avoid assuming detector orientation; ~0.99 for quantitative work. |
34	
35	**Geometry** (needed to build the q-map): dist 190 mm, λ 1.2915 Å (9.6 keV), beam center
36	(35.51, −35.22) mm, 75 µm pixels, `rot1=rot2=rot3=0`. Verified against stored `matrix_q`
37	to 4×10⁻¹² Å⁻¹.
38	
39	## Result (Run0475)

41	9 696 / 1 048 576 ≈ **0.925 %** masked — bad columns, hotspots, and Bragg spots from large
42	grains sitting on the rings.
43	
44	## When to use
45	
46	Cleaning an isotropic/amorphous or powder background where azimuthal symmetry holds; catches
47	dynamic outliers (cosmics, sporadic Bragg) that dark masks cannot.
48	
49	## Trade-offs
50	
51	**Will remove real anisotropic signal** (single-crystal Bragg, texture). Requires correct
52	geometry (dist, λ, beam center) to build the q-map.

3	description: RMM (Robust Mask Maker, Sadri 2022) dark-based mask — robustly models normal pixels per ASIC block from calibration constants and flags offset (Feature 2) and noise (Feature 3) outliers. Signal-independent, so it removes detector defects while preserving all diffraction signal. Preferred default defect mask.
4	---
5	
6	# Masking · Method 3 — RMM dark-based mask (robust statistics on calibration)
7	
8	**Family:** signal-independent. **Part of:** [masking](README.md).
9	
10	## Principle
11	
12	From Sadri et al., *J. Appl. Cryst.* **55**, 1549 (2022). Don't model bad pixels — robustly
13	model *normal* pixels. For a feature `x(i)`, fit a robust Gaussian (robust mean μ_R, robust
14	scale σ_R via the MSSE estimator, which uses only inliers so bad pixels don't pollute the fit),
15	then `SNR(i) = (x(i) − μ_R)/σ_R`; flag `|SNR| > λ`.
16	
17	Applied per **ASIC block (256×256)** so offset/noise are compared locally. Two features from
18	the calibration constants:
19	
20	| Feature | Input | Catches |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| **F2 — pixel offset** | pedestal (`ped[gain0]`) | anomalous bias; dead pixels (ped=0) |
23	| **F3 — pixel STD** | dark rms (`rms[gain0]`) | noisy/flickering (high) or dead (near-zero) pixels |
24	
25	Final mask = offset-outliers ∪ std-outliers.
26	
27	## Parameters
28	
29	| Param | Value | Why |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| `lambda_SNR` (λ) | 8.0 | Paper default `darkSNR=8`; conservative, only true outliers. Smaller ⇒ more aggressive. |
32	| `MSSE_LAMBDA` | 4.0 | Inlier cutoff *inside* the robust fit (paper default). |
33	| `asic_block` | 256 | Jungfrau ASIC size — the natural local unit for offset/noise. |
34	| `gain_stage` | 0 (high gain) | Stage actually used in this low-flux run; union across stages for completeness. |
35	
36	## Result (Run0475)
37	
38	2 363 / 1 048 576 ≈ **0.225 %** (offset-high 1231, offset-low 1, std-high 565, std-low 566).
39	Overlaps the [pyFAI mask](02_pyfai_azimuthal_sigmaclip.md) on 1661 pixels (the "smoking-gun"
40	bad ASIC band); 702 RMM-only pixels are calibration-bad but invisible in the average image;
41	the ~8035 pyFAI-only pixels are real Bragg/texture signal, not defects — so to remove defects
42	and keep signal, prefer this mask.
43	
44	## When to use
45	
46	You want to remove **detector defects while preserving all diffraction signal** — this is
47	signal-independent, so it never eats Bragg peaks. Preferred default defect mask.
48	
49	## Trade-offs
50	
51	Needs dark calibration inputs; static between calibrations; won't catch pixels that only
52	misbehave under illumination (→ [Feature-6](04_rmm_feature6_light.md)).
53	
54	## Repo
55	
56	`masking_RMM_darkbased/` — `build_rmm_mask.py`, `rmm_mask.npz`, `README_RMM方法说明.md`.
57	Install: `pip install RobustGaussianFittingLibrary`. On Apple Silicon the bundled `RGFLib.so`
58	is a Windows DLL — recompile the C core once:
59	`cc -O3 -fPIC -shared -o RGFLib.so RGFLib.c -lm`.

3	description: RMM Feature-6 mask — catches pixels that pass dark tests (F2/F3) but are persistently high/low under illumination, via a local robust plane fit and per-pixel SNR. Use when you suspect illumination-dependent bad pixels. Note the faithful version needs per-frame images (psana); the local approximation here uses the run-average image.
4	---
5	
6	# Masking · Method 4 — RMM Feature-6 mask (robust statistics under illumination)
7	
8	**Family:** signal-independent. **Part of:** [masking](README.md).
9	
10	## Principle
11	
12	From Sadri et al. (2022). Some pixels look fine in the dark (F2/F3 pass) but are persistently
13	high/low **when illuminated**. For each pixel, robustly fit a plane to a local window, take the
14	pixel's SNR vs that local background, average over frames, then run outlier detection on that
15	map (`|SNR| > λ` ⇒ bad).
16	
17	## Parameters
18	
19	| Param | Value | Why |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| `window` | 15×15 | Paper-recommended local window (~225 px, robust). |
22	| `numModelParams` | 4 | Local background = plane / low-order surface. |
23	| `MSSE_LAMBDA` | 3.0 | Inlier cutoff for the local plane fit. |
24	| `asic_block` | 256 | Grouping unit for the outlier-detection stage (Jungfrau ASIC). |
25	| `lambda_SNR` (λ) | 8.0 | Final flag threshold, consistent with F2/F3. |
26	
27	## Result (Run0475)
28	
29	1 635 / 1 048 576 ≈ **0.156 %** (persistently bright 668, dark/dead 967).
30	
31	## When to use
32	
33	You suspect illumination-dependent bad pixels (flickers, response nonlinearities) that dark
34	masks ([method 3](03_rmm_dark_based.md)) miss.
35	
36	## Trade-offs / caveat
37	
38	The faithful version needs **per-frame 2D images** (raw XTC via `psana`, Linux-only). This
39	machine's approximation runs the *identical* math on the whole-run **average** image, so it
40	catches pixels *persistently* anomalous vs their neighborhood but **not** intermittent
41	flickers. State this limitation when reporting.
42	
43	## Repo
44	
45	`masking_RMM_feature6_light/` — `build_feature6.py`, `feature6.npz`, `README_Feature6说明.md`.

# Mask Rationale — Run 475 (Jungfrau1M, LaB6)

**Image:** `sum_assembled.npy` (1064 x 1030), float64 sum of 1781 kept, calibrated,
normalised shots.  
**Mask:** `mask_assembled.npy` (1064 x 1030), bool, `True = masked`.  
**Total masked:** 102 416 / 1 095 920 pixels (9.35% of assembled image; **5.25% of
physical panel area**).  
**Usable detector area:** 993 504 pixels (94.8% of panel area).

---

## Layer-by-layer breakdown

### Layer 1 — Geometry gaps + 1-pixel dilation

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Core gap pixels (img == 0) | 47 369 (4.32%) |
| After 1-pixel dilation (3x3 structuring element) | 59 802 |
| **New pixels added to mask** | **59 802** |

**What:** Every cell in the assembled image where no physical detector pixel exists
— inter-module gap (rows 514–549, 36 rows), intra-panel ASIC column gaps (cols
256–257, 514–515, 772–773), and intra-panel ASIC row gaps (rows 256–257,
806–807). These are exactly zero in the assembled sum.

**Why:** Gap cells contain no photon information; reading them as zero-intensity
would bias any azimuthal average or peak fit. The 1-pixel binary dilation (3x3
square structuring element, 1 iteration) serves two purposes:
1. **ASIC boundary double-intensity lines:** Edge pixels flanking the gaps
   (cols 255, 258, 513, 516, 771, 774; rows 255, 258, 513, 550, 805, 808)
   have ~2x elevated median intensity (e.g., col 255 median 621 vs col 254
   median 329) due to effective-area doubling at the ASIC boundary. The
   dilation automatically catches them.
2. **Unreliable gap-edge pixels:** Pixels at the exact boundary of physical
   panel edges may have partial charge sharing or geometric vignetting.

**Trade-off:** The dilation masks ~12 400 real detector pixels beyond the raw gap,
but these are the known-biased ASIC boundary lines. The cost (1.2% of panel area)
is justified by eliminating the ~2x intensity bias they would inject.

**Note (Layer 4 subsumption):** ASIC boundary lines were also targeted explicitly
as Layer 4 (see below), but the dilation in this layer already covered 100% of
them, so Layer 4 added 0 new pixels.

---

### Layer 2 — Dead/stuck pixels (strongly negative, < −100)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Strongly negative pixels (val < −100) | 3 844 raw |
| **New pixels added to mask** | **3 784** |

**What:** Pixels with calibrated sum < −100. These include:
- 601 pixels with extreme values < −1000 (down to −4.3 × 10⁸), concentrated at
  specific columns (172–173, 633–634, 718–720) — stuck/dead pixels whose
  pedestal subtraction yields pathological results.
- ~3 200 pixels in the range [−1000, −100] — less extreme but still physically
  unreasonable in a sum of 1781 positive-signal shots.

**Why:** A physical sum of normalised LaB6 scattering shots cannot be significantly
negative. The P50 of the good (nonzero, non-gap) image is ~332; pixels at −100
are > 1σ below zero. These are defective pixels whose calibration fails.

**Mildly negative pixels not masked:** 10 739 pixels in (−100, 0) were examined
and found to be 86.1% isolated single pixels (8 424 connected components, median
cluster size = 1, max cluster = 19). This is consistent with statistical noise
in the pedestal-subtracted, normalised sum — not structured defects. Masking them
would remove ~1% of detector area unnecessarily.

**Trade-off:** The −100 threshold is conservative; a few mildly defective pixels
in (−100, 0) may survive. This is preferable to false-positive masking of noise
fluctuations.

### Layer 3 — Known-bad pixels (`status_bad.npy`)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Bad pixels in raw space | 4 565 |
| Mapped to assembled coordinates | 4 565 |
| **New pixels added to mask** | **2 687** |

coordinate maps.

**Why:** Factory characterisation identifies pixels with anomalous gain, dark
current, or connectivity issues. This is Method 00 from the masking skill set —
the always-on baseline that every other mask unions onto.

**Overlap:** 1 878 of the 4 565 raw bad pixels were already masked by Layers 1–2
(gap-adjacent or strongly negative), leaving 2 687 novel. These are bad pixels
that happen to read near-normal values in the sum but are unreliable.
